theorem_title: Construct original-edge routes between all triangular-polytope vertices in at most the dimension many steps
formal_statement:
theorem Hirsch.triangular_polytope_original_edge_routes (e : ℝ) (he : 0 < e) (he2 : e < 1/2) (d : ℕ)
    (u v : Fin d → ℝ)
    (hu : u ∈ ({x : Fin d → ℝ | (∀ i, 0 ≤ x i ∧ x i ≤ 1) ∧
      ∀ (i j : Fin d), i.val+1=j.val → e*x j ≤ x i ∧ x i ≤ 1-e*x j}).extremePoints ℝ)
    (hv : v ∈ ({x : Fin d → ℝ | (∀ i, 0 ≤ x i ∧ x i ≤ 1) ∧
      ∀ (i j : Fin d), i.val+1=j.val → e*x j ≤ x i ∧ x i ≤ 1-e*x j}).extremePoints ℝ) :
    ∃ (N : ℕ) (p : ℕ → Fin d → ℝ), N ≤ d ∧ p 0=u ∧ p N=v ∧
      (∀ j, j ≤ N → p j ∈
        ({x : Fin d → ℝ | (∀ i, 0 ≤ x i ∧ x i ≤ 1) ∧
          ∀ (i k : Fin d), i.val+1=k.val → e*x k ≤ x i ∧ x i ≤ 1-e*x k}).extremePoints ℝ) ∧
      ∀ j, j < N → p j ≠ p (j+1) ∧
        IsExtreme ℝ
          {x : Fin d → ℝ | (∀ i, 0 ≤ x i ∧ x i ≤ 1) ∧
            ∀ (i k : Fin d), i.val+1=k.val → e*x k ≤ x i ∧ x i ≤ 1-e*x k}
          (segment ℝ (p j) (p (j+1))) := by sorry
natural_language_statement: For every real 0<e<1/2, every natural dimension d (including zero), and ANY two actual extreme points u,v of the explicit triangular inequality set, construct a path of length at most d between them. Every path point is an extreme point of the same original set and every step has distinct endpoints and is a Mathlib extreme segment of that set, hence a genuine original ordinary edge. The set is defined by 0<=x_i<=1 and e*x_j<=x_i<=1-e*x_j whenever j=i+1. Neither a Boolean labeling of the endpoints, completeness of a vertex list, an adjacency oracle, nor a bounded path is assumed. The proof classifies all extreme points by recursive lower/upper choices, proves lower/upper affine lifts preserve extreme sets, proves the vertical fibre over an extreme tail is an extreme segment, and recursively constructs the path. This is a positive original-edge route theorem for the classical triangular family, not a graph-distance lower bound and not an unrestricted proof of Polynomial Hirsch. The public theorem asserts an upper bound, not shortestness or nonrevisiting for arbitrary routes.

Classical triangular family and hypercube graph: Gaertner, Helbling, Ota, Takahashi, Large Shadows from Sparse Inequalities, arXiv:1308.2495v1 Section4. No historical novelty claim.
